{{Short description|Mathematical index used in Bayesian statistics}}

In [[Bayesian statistics|Bayesian]] [[statistics]], the '''probability of direction''' ('''''pd''''') is a measure of effect existence representing the certainty with which an effect is positive or negative.<ref name="makowski2019bayestestR">{{cite journal |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan |last3=Lüdecke |first3=Daniel |title=bayestestR: Describing Effects and their Uncertainty, Existence and Significance within the Bayesian Framework |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=13 August 2019 |volume=4 |issue=40 |page=1541 |doi=10.21105/joss.01541|bibcode=2019JOSS....4.1541M |s2cid=201882316 |doi-access=free }}</ref> This index is numerically similar to the frequentist [[p-value |''p''-value]].<ref name="makowski2019indices">{{cite journal |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan S. |last3=Chen |first3=S. H. Annabel |last4=Lüdecke |first4=Daniel |title=Indices of Effect Existence and Significance in the Bayesian Framework |journal=Frontiers in Psychology |date=10 December 2019 |volume=10 |page=2767 |doi=10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02767|pmid=31920819 |pmc=6914840 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Heiss |first1=Andrew |title=Bayesian statistics resources |url=https://evalf21.classes.andrewheiss.com/resource/bayes/#probability-of-direction |website=Georgia State University - Bayesian statistics course |access-date=7 December 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref>

==Definition==
It is mathematically defined as the larger of two [[Posterior probability|posterior probabilities:]] the probability of the parameter (<math>\theta</math>) being negative and the probability of the parameter being positive:<math display="block">pd=\text{max}\{Pr(\theta<0), Pr(\theta>0)\}</math>When the posterior is a ''continuous'' distribution, this value is also equal the proportion of the posterior distribution that is of the median's sign, and varies between 50% and 100%.<ref name="kelter2020analysis">{{cite journal |last1=Kelter |first1=Riko |title=Analysis of Bayesian posterior significance and effect size indices for the two-sample t-test to support reproducible medical research |journal=BMC Medical Research Methodology |date=December 2020 |volume=20 |issue=1 |page=88 |doi=10.1186/s12874-020-00968-2 |pmid=32321438 |pmc=7178740 |doi-access=free }}</ref> However, when the posterior is a ''discrete'' distribution (or a ''mixture'' of continuous and discrete values), this value might not be equal to the proportion of the posterior distribution that is of the median's sign (as the median might be equal to the null value), and can be as low as 0% (when the null has a 100% posterior probability).

==History==
The original formulation of this index and its usage in [[Bayesian statistics]] can be found in the [[Psycho (software)|psycho]] software documentation by [[Dominique Makowski]] under the appellation ''Maximum Probability of Effect'' (MPE).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |title=The psycho Package: an Efficient and Publishing-Oriented Workflow for Psychological Science |journal=The Journal of Open Source Software |date=5 February 2018 |volume=3 |issue=22 |page=470 |doi=10.21105/joss.00470 |bibcode=2018JOSS....3..470M |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |title=psycho - The Bayesian Framework |url=https://cran.r-hub.io/web/packages/psycho/vignettes/bayesian.html |website=cran.r-hub.io |access-date=26 November 2021}}</ref> It was later renamed ''Probability of Direction'' and implemented in the [[easystats]] collection of software. Similar formulations have also been described in the context of bootstrapped parameters interpretation.{{Citation needed|date=November 2021}}

==Properties==

The probability of direction is easy to estimate, is typically independent of the specific parameterization of the model or scaling of the predictor(s) or outcome, and is not sensitive to prior specification (insofar as the posterior is not prior specification).

Advantages and limitations of the probability of direction have been studied by comparing it to other indices including the Bayes factor or Bayesian [[Equivalence test]]:<ref name="makowski2019indices" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baig |first1=Sabeeh A |title=Bayesian Inference: Parameter Estimation for Inference in Small Samples |journal=Nicotine & Tobacco Research |date=22 October 2021 |volume=24 |issue=6 |pages=937–941 |doi=10.1093/ntr/ntab221|pmid=34679175 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="kelter2020analysis" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kelter |first1=Riko |title=Bayesian and frequentist testing for differences between two groups with parametric and nonparametric two-sample tests |journal=WIREs Computational Statistics |date=2021 |volume=13 |issue=6 |article-number=e1523 |doi=10.1002/wics.1523 |s2cid=225532985 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Unlike indices related to the [[Region of Practical Interest]] (ROPE; where rescaling a variable requires rescaling the ROPE), its computation is not sensitive to the scale of the response or predictor variables. Unlike the [[Bayes factor]] - an index of relative fit of the prior model - the probability of direction it is an index of the [[posterior distribution]]. Like the ROPE and unlike the Bayes factor, the probability of direction can easily be estimated from [[Markov chain Monte Carlo|MCMC]] samples by counting the proportion of samples that are larger than the null and the proportion of samples smaller than the null, and taking the larger of the two.

However, similarly to its frequentist counterpart - the ''p''-value - this index is not able to quantify evidence ''in favor'' of the null hypothesis since in most applied cases it cannot be lower than 50% (see above).<ref name="makowski2019indices" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kelter |first1=Riko |title=How to Choose between Different Bayesian Posterior Indices for Hypothesis Testing in Practice |journal=Multivariate Behavioral Research |date=28 September 2021 |volume=58 |issue=1 |pages=160–188 |doi=10.1080/00273171.2021.1967716|pmid=34582284 |arxiv=2005.13181 |s2cid=218900848 }}</ref>

==Relationship with ''p''-value==

In cases that produce posterior distributions that are close in shape to frequentists sampling distributions (such as the conditions required for the [[Bernstein–von Mises theorem]]) the probability of direction has a direct correspondence with the frequentist one-sided ''p''-value through the formula <math>p_\text{one-sided} = 1 - pd</math> and to the two-sided ''p''-value through the formula <math>p_\text{two-sided} = 2 \left(1 - pd\right)</math>. Thus, a two-sided ''p''-value of respectively .1, .05, .01 and .001 would correspond approximately to a ''pd'' of 95%, 97.5%, 99.5% and 99.95%.<ref>{{cite web |title=BayestestR - Probability of Direction |url=https://easystats.github.io/bayestestR/reference/p_direction.html |website=easystats.github.io/bayestestR |access-date=26 November 2021 |ref=bayestestRdocs |language=en}}</ref> The proximity between the ''pd'' and the ''p''-value is in line with the interpretation of the former as an index of effect existence, as it follows the original definition of the ''p''-value.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Fisher |first1=R. A. |title=Statistical methods for research workers (11th ed. rev.) |date=1925 |publisher=Oliver and Boyd |location=Edinburgh}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cohen |first1=Jacob |title=The earth is round (p < .05). |journal=American Psychologist |date=1994 |volume=49 |issue=12 |pages=997–1003 |doi=10.1037/0003-066X.49.12.997}}</ref>

==Interpretation==
The probability of direction can be interpreted as a continuous measure of evidence, without "testing" it against a fixed threshold.

However, for instances where a decision is ''required'', the [[easystats|bayestestR]] package for [[R (programming language)|R]] suggests the following rule of thumb guidelines, based on the association between it and the frequentist ''p''-value:<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayesian Reporting Guidelines |url=https://easystats.github.io/bayestestR/articles/guidelines.html |website=easystats.github.io/bayestestR |access-date=26 November 2021 |ref=bayestestRguidelines |language=en}}</ref>

{{alternating rows table|class=wikitable}}
! '''''pd''''' !! ''p''-value equivalence !! Interpretation
|-
| <math>\leq 95\%</math> || <math>p > .1</math> || Uncertain
|-
| <math>> 95\%</math> || <math>p < .1</math> || Possibly existing
|-
| <math>> 97\%</math> || <math>p < .06</math> || Likely existing
|-
| <math>> 99\%</math> || <math>p < .02</math> || Probably existing
|-
| <math>> 99.9\%</math> || <math>p < .002</math> || Certainly existing
|-
|}
